biography: Born in Madrid, Antonio García's racing journey began not on a karting track, but on the winding roads of the Sierra de Guadarrama. His father, a rally enthusiast, instilled in him a deep appreciation for car control and strategy. At age 16, he entered a local karting series, quickly proving his talent. A defining moment came at the Spanish National Karting Championship, where a daring last-lap overtake secured him the title, catching the attention of a Formula Ford team. After a few successful seasons in feeder series, García transitioned to GT racing, finding a home and consistent success with Chevrolet. Currently, he's a linchpin of their endurance racing program, known for his calculated approach and consistent performance, aiming for another major endurance victory to cement his legacy.
drivingStyle: García is a master of consistency and tire management. He doesn't often make flashy overtakes, preferring to set up his passes meticulously, exploiting the smallest weaknesses in his opponents' defenses. He possesses an uncanny ability to conserve his tires, often running longer stints than his rivals without a significant drop in pace. Under pressure, García remains remarkably calm, rarely making mistakes and capitalizing on the errors of others. His smooth inputs and intelligent racecraft make him a formidable competitor in any endurance event.

rivalries.reason: A long-standing rivalry stemming from their days in Formula Ford, Bellini's aggressive style clashes with García's calculated approach, leading to several on-track incidents.

Dubois, a rising star in GT racing, often challenges García for the lead in endurance races. Their rivalry is based on mutual respect, but both are fiercely competitive, pushing each other to the limit.
Tanaka and Garcia have a rivalry in GTE Pro due to their different driving styles. Tanaka is very aggressive, while Garcia is much more calculated. This has led to some very close battles.

quirks: Always wears the same pair of lucky socks, inherited from his grandfather, during race weekends.
Studies historical race footage of the track he's racing on the night before each race.
Listens to classical guitar music to calm his nerves before getting into the car.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't just about speed; it's about understanding the chessboard and making the right moves at the right time."
careerHighlight: Winning the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2020 with Chevrolet, after a strategic masterclass of fuel saving and consistent lap times, securing victory in the final hour.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 24 Hours of Daytona in 2018 due to a mechanical failure with only 30 minutes left, costing him and his team a likely victory.
